title: A/B Symmetric Metamorphic Relations for Position/Framing Bias in Honesty

original_idea.body:
# A/B Symmetric Metamorphic Relations for Position/Framing Bias in Honesty

**Problem:** Models may give different factual verdicts depending on answer ordering or framing (positive vs negative phrasing), revealing that the 'honest' answer is an artifact of framing rather than belief.

**Direction:** Apply symmetric metamorphic relations (proven for code-generation stability) to honesty: for each factual claim, generate symmetric variants (claim vs negated claim; option A first vs swapped). The MR is 'truth verdict must be logically consistent under symmetry.' Measure violation rate as a 'framing-honesty' instability index across open models.

**Why it matters:** Reveals whether stated beliefs are stable or framing-dependent — a basic honesty property. Symmetric MRs are oracle-free and trivially automatable, ideal for a 30-hour counterfactual project.

**Relevant context:** Symmetric MRs validate code-generation stability via source/follow-up violation detection (ScienceDirect S0164121224003741; arXiv:2505.07870 prioritizing MRs). Sycophancy/framing effects documented (ELEPHANT arXiv:2505.13995).
